v1_benchmark.role: benchmark only; not grandfathered as champion

current_findings_that_motivate_v2: V1 full-universe headline errors were materially better than meaningful-starter slices because easy zero/nonparticipant rows diluted error.
V1 meaningful-player central projection accuracy was not strong enough for the intended product.
Many richer matchup/efficiency candidates were correctly rejected in V1, leaving several offensive efficiency heads at simple B0 formulations.
The rejected V1 dynamic game-script implementation does not prove game script is unimportant; it proves that implementation was not good enough.
Monte Carlo must be downstream of a direct football projection.
open_research_tracks: receiving matchup mechanics: depth-of-target, explosives, pressure/blitz, timestamp-safe coverage tendency, player-vs-scheme splits
defensive personnel absence features with timing-safe routing
frozen_or_blocked: 65% alt line presentation is not evidence of projection quality
offensive-line quality features blocked until a timestamp-safe source is available
Phase 1C-T generic PBP team-environment candidate frozen; no general promotion
Phase 1D-R generic QB attempt-share allocator rejected; QB needs dedicated starter/replacement logic
next_milestone: V2 Phase 1H-R: receiving matchup mechanics using genuinely new PBP/FTN/coverage information, routed into catch/air/YAC components and selected on 2024 component accuracy before 2025 validation.

phase0_week4.primary_failure_signal: opportunity volume/role is a major upstream error source; receiving/pass opportunity requires first V2 rebuild

phase1c_team_environment.conclusion: PBP structure beat dumb recent-volume baselines but did not consistently beat the simpler Phase1B team-volume layer out of time.

phase1d_role_allocation.conclusion: Target-share and carry-share allocation improved honestly on 2025 validation; generic QB share allocation failed and is rejected.

competent_human_benchmark.rule: Every sophisticated V2 central-projection candidate must materially beat this benchmark as well as strong simple/V1 baselines.

phase1e_integrated.conclusion: Coherent receiving/rushing role allocation improved 2025 final projections and player opportunities; rushing also improved materially in 2026 burned diagnostics. Receiving yards was essentially flat/slightly worse than Phase1B on 2026 W1-4, so its final head remains research.

phase1f_efficiency_forensic.conclusion: Both opportunity and efficiency materially limit receiving/rushing; human-efficiency swap rejected because direct efficiency/oracle-workload metrics were worse despite tiny receiving-yard final cancellation gain.

phase1g_receiving_mechanics.conclusion: Catch/air/YAC decomposition is retained as architecture, but simple opponent-position blending is worse than incumbent under oracle workload and its tiny final gain is immaterial.
